title: Defending the note's feeling became a where-were-you roll call
happened: The note opens with two paragraphs of feeling: the mathematician writes that Claude 'flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line'. Many people mocked the prose that afternoon (those posts are marked or left out below). A set of members answered the mockery. hotrollhottakes posted the question he thought the mathematician was testing; shibbi replied that mathematicians being weird and rhapsodic is a time-honoured tradition, and that he is too; shimmermathlabs asked whether people really thought it cringe and said she would remember where she was when she first saw the PDF: in bed, thinking about making donuts. Later she asked outright, 'where were you when you realized the riemann hypothesis was true?', and posted a photo of her two homemade 'riemann hypothesis donuts'. People answered: in a bath, on the couch scrolling when they should have been working, in a computer chair in a hoodie, just waking up, 'at house eating dorito' (a phrase echoing an older copypasta, which a non-member had also used that afternoon as 'where were you wen RH die'). Separately, a small member, astra.cam, replied to a non-member who had said the mathematician should have stopped at the first paragraph: a mathematician who chased the problem all his life is surely allowed a few paragraphs of exuberance. The non-member replied 'Awww now I feel bad' with applause, and astra.cam added that it was nice to see a remark.pdf written by an excited mathematician rather than a PR team. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.

couldBeShown: The donuts (her alt text, confirmed by the skeleton): a cup of coffee next to a pink plate with two slightly misshapen homemade donut holes covered in sugar, on a wood-pattern table. The note's first page (zachweinersmith's image, no alt, fetched): two paragraphs of the PDF in a serif typeface, beginning 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis' and including 'Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.' It is the mathematician's own text and outside the community. The roll call itself is a list of places (bed, bath, couch, computer chair, waking up, eating Doritos) that could be shown as answers to one question.
notUnderstood: The 'where were you wen ... die' copypasta and 'at house eating dorito': a known meme format; its origin is not established from the data, and one well-known version is about a death. nwclerk1337's version is about the hypothesis 'dying'.
Whether the mathematician would be glad to see his prose discussed at all; he is outside the community.
shimmermathlabs' 'tetrahedron in my hair' is presumably literal; not checked.
sensitive: The mathematician (Levent Alpöge) is a real person outside the community (R1, R7, repost test). The note's prose is his; the show may show the community's posts about it, never mock his state of mind.
